claim_review.source: ASI, Excavations at Udayagiri-2 (1997–2000), title and printed p.4
claim_review.finding: The title, author and 2007 edition match. Printed p.4 identifies Alti/Nalti, Assia and Mahavinayaka as regional hill-range wings. The draft does not transfer Udayagiri monastery dates, Buddhist origins, rivers, fauna, routes or horseshoe formation to Mahavinayak.

claim_review.source: Gouri Kumar Brahma, Odisha Review May–June 2015, printed pp.58, 62–63
claim_review.finding: Title and author inspected; printed p.62 supports the single monolith and five named deities, with portions assigned to each. Printed p.63 explicitly says reprinted from July 1969. Draft attributes the interpretation to Brahma and does not adopt his thousand-year age statement or outdated Cuttack/railway geography.

claim_review.source: R. K. Periwal, Siva Temples of South India, imprint and printed pp.4–5
claim_review.finding: 1995 compiler/publisher imprint inspected. Printed p.4 introduces Chandikhol and two temples; p.5 separately identifies Chandi and Mahavinayak, five divine forms and a hill-fed stream. Draft states the stream as a dated guide account and omits perennial flow, old travel distances, accommodation and meditation guarantees.

claim_review.source: Odisha Tourism, April 2026 identified centres, printed p.4
claim_review.finding: Mahavinayak appears as Jajpur item08, Religious Centre. Draft uses pilgrimage/hill-shrine framing, not an unsupported hill-station category.

Fresh independent official-domain indexed result identifies Parbat Sova at Mahavinayak and a stay listing. Direct EcoTour opening returned a JavaScript shell. This supports the narrow official listing and checking advice; no rendered booking, availability, prices, services or field observation verified.

editorial.finding: Original compact synthesis with clear attribution, plain headings and a practical distinction between neighbouring shrines. Some explanatory sentences reiterate the main point, but none requires correction. Temple photograph caption remains general and dated; no image-based identification of the sacred monolith or subsidiary shrine.
